summary: Benjamin Ide Wheeler was a linguist who studied at Brown and Heidelberg (Ph.D. under Hermann Osthoff). He taught at Brown, Harvard, Cornell (1886–1899), and served as professor and president of the University of California, Berkeley (1899–1919).

Benjamin Lewis Rice worked in Indology and archaeology. He served as Principal of the Central College of Bangalore (~1860–1865), Director of the Department of Public Instruction (~1868–1883), and Director of the Mysore Archaeological Department (~1884–1889).

Benjamin Rowland worked in archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his S.B. and Ph.D. at Harvard University, where he served as associate professor from 1930 to 1972 and curated Asian collections at the Fogg Art Museum.

Benjamin Schultze was an Indologist and linguist who studied theology at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1711). He served as a missionary with the Danish-Halle Mission (1719–1726) and the Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge (1728).
Benjamin W. Fortson IV is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Yale University (~1985–1989) and Harvard University (~1991–1996), and held a post at the University of Michigan (~2004).

Benjamin Wood specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Toronto under Frances Garrett and also studied under Khenpo Kunga Sherab, Shayne Clarke, and Thubten Champa.

Benkyo Shiio was a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate from the University of Tokyo (-1915). He lectured at Shukyo, Nihon, and Waseda universities, served as president of Taisho University (1926), and headed the Sanko Library and Research Institute.

Benoytosh Bhattacharyya was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Calcutta and the University of Dhaka. He served as General Editor of Gaekwad's Oriental Series (1924) and Director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (~1927–1952).

Benoît Vermander works in Sinology and religious studies. He studied at Yale, Sciences Po, Fu Jen Catholic University, and Centre Sèvres. He served as Academic Director of Taipei Ricci Institute (1996–2009) before joining Fudan University as professor in 2009.

Bernard Essers was a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He studied under Barend Faddegon and Johanna Engelberta van Lohuizen-de Leeuw at the University of Amsterdam, and completed his Th.D. at the University of Groningen under Theodorus Christiaan Vriezen (1952).

Bernard Faure specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. Educated at Sciences Po, INALCO, and the University of Paris (Doctorat d'État, 1984), he held faculty posts at Cornell (~1983–1987), Stanford (~1987–2006), and Columbia (~2006).

Bernard Frank was a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who studied under Rolf Alfred Stein. He served as head of Maison Franco-Japonaise (~1972–1974) and held the chair of Civilisation japonaise at the Collège de France (1979–1996).
Bernard Goldman was a scholar of archaeology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Michigan and held a post at Wayne State University from ~1956 to 1986.
Bernard Pignède was a scholar in Tibetology and other fields. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Louis Dumont from ~1956 to 1960.

Bernard S. Cohn was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and Cornell University (Ph.D.), he taught at the University of Rochester (1960–1964) and the University of Chicago (1956–1960, 1964–1995).

Bernard Williams was a philosopher who studied at Chigwell School and Balliol College, Oxford (~1947–1951). He held academic posts at University College London (~1964–1967) and the University of California, Berkeley (~1988–2003).

Bernd Barschel was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg and the University of Jena (Ph.D. 1976), holding posts as Assistant at Halle-Wittenberg (1960–1970) and Lektor at Jena (1977).
Bernd Schneidmüller is a historian who held academic posts at the University of Oldenburg (~1992–1994) and Heidelberg University (~2003).

Bernfried Schlerath was a linguist and scholar of Indology and Iranian studies. He earned his Ph.D. under Hermann Lommel at Frankfurt, later serving as professor at the University of Marburg (1970) and the Free University of Berlin (1974–1992).

Bernhard Breloer was an Indologist and philosopher who earned a Ph.D. and Dr.iuris at Bonn under Hermann Jacobi and Willibald Kirfel. He was a Privatdozent at Bonn (1927) and Dean of faculty at Humboldt University of Berlin (1935).
